version: "0.1"
title: Directory Organizer
objective: >-
  A single-file, stdlib-only Python program (organizer.py) that moves files from the top level of a target
  directory into subdirectories named after their extension, either once (--once) or continuously (--watch),
  logging every move to organizer.log.
execution_mode: critical
context:
  system: "Empty Python project; a single module organizer.py at the repository root, tests under tests/ with unittest."
  assumptions:
    - "The subdirectory name is the lowercased extension without the dot (report.PDF goes to pdf/); a file with no extension goes to no_extension/."
    - "Only the last suffix counts (archive.tar.gz goes to gz/)."
    - "Watch mode polls the directory at a fixed interval (default 2 seconds, --interval); no third-party filesystem events library."
    - "The target directory is a positional argument; organizer.log is written in the current working directory unless --log is given, and is never moved."
    - "On a name collision in the destination the file is renamed with a numeric suffix (a.txt becomes a_1.txt); nothing is overwritten."
    - "Only regular files are moved; directories and symlinks are left untouched."
constraints:
  - "Python standard library only; no third-party packages."
  - "Everything lives in one file, organizer.py."
  - "Never recurse into subdirectories and never touch files already inside them."
  - "Never move hidden files (names starting with a dot)."
  - "Never overwrite an existing file."
  - "No deletion of files and no GUI or daemonization."
success_criteria:
  - "--once organizes the top level of the target and exits with code 0."
  - "--watch keeps organizing files that appear later until interrupted with Ctrl+C."
  - "Each move appends one line to organizer.log with a timestamp, source and destination."
  - "Hidden files and files in subdirectories are left where they are."
hypotheses:
  - {id: h1, description: "A visible top-level file is moved into a subdirectory named after its lowercased extension, and into no_extension when it has none.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h2, description: "Hidden files and files already in subdirectories are never moved.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h3, description: "--once performs one pass and exits, while --watch keeps organizing new files until interrupted.", confidence: 0.85}
  - {id: h4, description: "Every move is appended to organizer.log with timestamp, source and destination.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h5, description: "A destination name collision never overwrites an existing file.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h6, description: "The CLI requires exactly one of --once or --watch and a target directory, and exits with code 2 on an invalid target.", confidence: 0.85}
required_evidence:
  - "unittest run of tests/ showing all boundary tests passing"
  - "gate output ending in RESULT: PASS"
actions:
  - {id: a1, description: "Implement organizer.py with classification, move and log logic", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2, h4, h5]}
  - {id: a2, description: "Implement the CLI and the once/watch loop", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h3, h6]}
  - {id: a3, description: "Write unittest boundary tests for every obligation and run the gate", type: test, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6]}
decision_rules:
  - "If a behavior is not covered by an obligation, stop and propose a spec amendment."
  - "If the gate fails, fix the implementation, never the approved tests."
metadata:
  source_prompt: "Build a Directory Organizer in Python. Watch a target directory and move files into subdirectories by extension. Two modes: --watch and --once. Log moves to organizer.log. Skip files already in subdirs and hidden files. Single file organizer.py, stdlib only."
  generator: claude-code-session
  scope_contract:
    must_include:
      - "move files by extension"
      - "--once mode"
      - "--watch mode"
      - "log moves to organizer.log"
      - "skip files already in subdirs"
      - "skip hidden files"
      - "single file organizer.py"
      - "stdlib only"
scope:
  paths: ["organizer.py", "tests/**"]
  tests: tests
formal:
  module: DirOrganizer
  obligations:
    - id: move_by_extension
      kind: boundary
      statement: "A visible top-level file moves to a subdirectory named by its lowercased extension (no_extension when none); a name collision gets a numeric suffix and never overwrites."
      hypotheses: [h1, h5]
      must_include: ["move files by extension"]
      test: "test_organizer.OrganizeTests.test_moves_by_extension"
    - id: once_mode
      kind: boundary
      statement: "--once does a single pass over the target and exits 0."
      hypotheses: [h3, h6]
      must_include: ["--once mode"]
      test: "test_organizer.CliTests.test_once_exits_zero"
    - id: watch_mode
      kind: boundary
      statement: "--watch keeps organizing files that appear after start until stopped."
      hypotheses: [h3]
      must_include: ["--watch mode"]
      test: "test_organizer.WatchTests.test_watch_organizes_new_files"
    - id: log_moves
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Each move appends a line with timestamp, source and destination to organizer.log."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["log moves to organizer.log"]
      test: "test_organizer.LogTests.test_move_is_logged"
    - id: skip_subdirs
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Files inside subdirectories are not touched and nothing is recursed into."
      hypotheses: [h2]
      must_include: ["skip files already in subdirs"]
      test: "test_organizer.OrganizeTests.test_skips_files_in_subdirs"
    - id: skip_hidden
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Files whose names start with a dot stay in place."
      hypotheses: [h2]
      must_include: ["skip hidden files"]
      test: "test_organizer.OrganizeTests.test_skips_hidden_files"
    - id: single_file
      kind: boundary
      statement: "organizer.py is one self-contained module that is runnable as a script."
      hypotheses: [h6]
      must_include: ["single file organizer.py"]
      test: "test_organizer.CliTests.test_single_file_script_runs"
    - id: stdlib_only
      kind: boundary
      statement: "organizer.py imports only standard library modules."
      hypotheses: [h6]
      must_include: ["stdlib only"]
      test: "test_organizer.CliTests.test_imports_are_stdlib_only"
EOF

**Approving this spec bundle** (`forgemyspec-bundle/dir-organizer/`) approves the following. It is a spec-only bundle: no Dafny contract, only Python boundary tests.

- **Behavior:** `organizer.py` takes a target directory plus `--once` or `--watch`.
  - It moves top-level files into `<lowercased-ext>/`, or `no_extension/` when there is no extension. Only the last suffix counts, so `archive.tar.gz` goes to `gz/`.
  - Hidden files, files already in subdirs, directories and symlinks are skipped.
  - A name collision gets a numeric suffix (`a.txt` becomes `a_1.txt`) and nothing is overwritten.
  - `--watch` polls every 2 seconds; `--interval` changes that.
- **Log:** moves are appended to `organizer.log` in the current directory. `--log` overrides the path. The log file is never moved.
- **Invalid target:** exits with code 2.
- **Tests:** 8 boundary tests, one per obligation, covering each must-include phrase.
- **Assumptions I made that you may want to change:** polling instead of filesystem events, the log location, and the collision suffix.
- **Scope:** `organizer.py` and `tests/**` only.
